thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Market Loses Steam After Jobs Report; Apple Sinks On Outlook

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Market Loses Steam After Jobs Report; Apple Sinks On Outlook
text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch , Chris Matthews
U.S. officials reject possibility of early resolution to trade war
Stocks are trading lower Friday, erasing an early rally that saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average surge nearly 200 points, as stronger-than expected jobs report reaffirmed the consensus that the Federal Reserve will again raise interest rates soon.
Expectations for a near-term resolution to the continuing U.S.-China trade war were dashed after several high-level government officials, including economic adviser to the president Larry Kudlow, rejected speculation of an imminent deal.
How are benchmarks faring?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 197 points, or 0.8%, to 25,183, the S&P 500 index fell 28 points, or 1.1%, to 2,711, while the Nasdaq Composite Index declined 99 points, or 1.3%, to 7,335.
What's driving the market?
The U.S. and China are a long way from reaching a trade deal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-china-trade-deal-seen-as-far-off-official-tells-cnbc-2018-11-02), according to one senior Trump administration official.
Kudlow, during an interview with CNBC, also stated that the president didn't request the drafting of trade accord (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stocks-skid-to-session-lows-as-kudlow-refutes-report-that-trump-asked-for-a-draft-of-a-china-us-trade-pact-2018-11-02) between the U.S. and China as reported by Bloomberg.
On Thursday, President Donald Trump tweeted that he had a "long and very good conversation" (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-today-president-suggests-progress-on-china-trade-after-talking-with-xi-2018-11-01) with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The phone conversations come ahead of a late-November meeting that is anticipated to take place on the sidelines of a G-20 summit of world leaders, where the pair could potentially iron out differences.
Opinion:On the economy and rate hikes, the Fed looks lost in the stars (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/on-the-economy-and-rate-hikes-the-fed-looks-lost-in-the-stars-2018-11-02)
On the data front, the U.S. economy added 250,000 new jobs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-250000-jobs-in-october-wages-rise-at-fastest-pace-in-more-than-nine-years-2018-11-02) in October, beating economists' expectations of 202,000. The unemployment rate remained flat at 3.7%, while the report showed year-over-year wage gains rising to 3.1%, slightly above the consensus estimate of 3%.
Stocks initially reacted well to the strong numbers but reversed direction as worries about tightening liquidity in the wake of a hawkish Fed seeped into market.
The U.S. trade deficit rose 1.3% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-imports-hit-all-time-high-trade-deficit-with-china-sets-new-record-despite-tariffs-2018-11-02) in September to a seven-month high as imports hit a record.
Which stocks are in focus?
Apple Inc.(AAPL) shares sank 7.3% after the tech giant posted results that were better than expected but disappointed on its outlook. It also said it would no longer disclose (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/when-the-going-gets-tough-apple-hides-its-numbers-2018-11-01) unit sales of its products for investors, as it has for more than a decade.
Arista Networks Inc. (ANET) stock rose 6.3% after the company reported better-than-expected earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/arista-stock-rallies-nearly-10-on-earnings-beat-2018-11-01).
Synchrony Financial(SYF) slumped 10%following reports that Walmart Inc. (WMT) is suing the company for breach of contract.
Shares of Starbucks Corp. (SBUX) shares rallied 8.6% after the firm posted same-store sales growth (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/higher-prices-boost-starbucks-to-record-sales-2018-11-01) of 4%.
Kraft Heinz Co. (KHC) skidded 9.4% after the food company missed Wall Street's profit estimates (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/kraft-heinz-shares-slump-on-weaker-than-expected-third-quarter-earnings-2018-11-01) in the third quarter.
Symantec Corp. (SYMC) rose 5.3% after reporting smaller losses than expected (following%20a%20Thursday%20evening%20earnings%20release%20that%20surpassed%20Wall%20Street%20expectations.).
Shares of Newell Brands Inc. (NWL) soared 14% after the consumer-goods company raised its full-year guidance for 2018 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/newell-brands-stock-jumps-after-adjusted-earnings-beat-raised-outlook-2018-11-02).
VeriSign Inc. (VRSN) stock rallied 15% after the company was upgraded by J.P. Morgan to neutral from underweight.
What are analysts saying?
Thomas Hainlin, global investment strategist with US Bank, said the market will remain volatile until concrete progress is made in U.S.-China trade relations. "If the two largest economies in the world can't agree on trade policy, that's not great for markets," he told MarketWatch.
"This sort of public posturing, private negotiation has been a tactic" the president has consistently used in trade negotiations, Hainlin said, suggesting that the midmorning downturn in the markets could be attributed to investors re-evaluating whether to take media reports on the president's plans at face value.
"This is a great jobs report," Randy Frederick, vice president of trading and derivatives at Charles Shwab. "Job growth was strong, and wage growth that shows we're making progress, but that runaway inflation isn't a concern," he said.
How are other markets trading?
Asian stock markets were up Friday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stock-markets-maintain-strong-november-start-2018-11-02), possibly reflecting renewed investor optimism that a U.S.-China trade pact can be reached. European stocks were also trading up on the day (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stock-markets-maintain-strong-november-start-2018-11-02).
Oil prices fell (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-crude-steadies-but-holds-at-april-lows-as-supply-remains-key-factor-2018-11-02) and the dollar ticked higher, while gold edged lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-hovers-near-3-month-high-2018-11-02).
--Mark DeCambre contributed to this article
